components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single bright next action in a surface or operational region.

components.name: Primary Navigation

components.name: Role Selector
components.description: Square operational role controls for choosing player or administrator access on the login surface.
components.html: Choose role
components.css: .ds-role-selector { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; gap: 10px; padding: 0; border: 0; color: var(--ink, #092f35); font-family: var(--font-body, 'Barlow', system-ui, sans-serif); } .ds-role-selector legend { grid-column: 1 / -1; margin-bottom: 10px; font-size: .78rem; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: .08em; } .ds-role-selector input { position: absolute; opacity: 0; } .ds-role-selector span { min-height: 76px; display: grid; align-content: center; padding: 16px; border: 1px solid rgba(9,47,53,.26); border-radius: 4px; cursor: pointer; font: 700 1.15rem/1 var(--font-display, 'Barlow Condensed', sans-serif); text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-role-selector small { margin-top: 6px; color: var(--ink-soft, #3e5c5d); font: 400 .77rem/1.2 var(--font-body, 'Barlow', system-ui, sans-serif); text-transform: none; } .ds-role-selector input:checked + span { color: var(--paper, #f5f2e9); background: var(--court, #0d3c36); border-color: var(--court, #0d3c36); box-shadow: inset 0 -4px 0 var(--mango, #f6b93b); } .ds-role-selector input:checked + span small { color: #d7e3df; } .ds-role-selector input:focus-visible + span { outline: 3px solid var(--focus, #7bb4ff); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Availability Marks
components.description: The fixed circle, triangle, and crossed-circle vocabulary for open, limited, and booked states.
components.html: OpenLimitedBooked
components.css: .ds-status-set { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 22px; padding: 16px; color: var(--ink, #092f35); background: var(--paper, #f5f2e9); font: 600 .86rem/1 var(--font-body, 'Barlow', system-ui, sans-serif); } .ds-status { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; } .ds-status-open, .ds-status-limited, .ds-status-booked { width: 28px; height: 28px; flex: 0 0 auto; } .ds-status-open { display: block; border: 4px solid var(--open, #14874e); border-radius: 50%; } .ds-status-limited { color: var(--limited, #996200); } .ds-status-booked { display: inline-grid; place-items: center; color: #fff; background: var(--booked, #b8253b); border-radius: 50%; } .ds-status-booked svg { width: 21px; height: 21px; }

components.name: Selected Court Slot
components.description: The signature selected state inside a sport-colored Courtline Scheduler lane.
components.css: .ds-slot-selected { min-height: 150px; min-width: 150px; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 12px; padding: 14px; color: #fff; background: var(--blue, #2367d1); border: 0; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 4px var(--paper, #f5f2e9); text-align: left; font-family: var(--font-body, 'Barlow', system-ui, sans-serif); cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 180ms ease-out, color 180ms ease-out, box-shadow 180ms ease-out; } .ds-slot-selected:hover { background: var(--blue-dark, #174ea9); } .ds-slot-selected:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--focus, #7bb4ff); outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-slot-selected > span:last-child { display: grid; gap: 4px; } .ds-slot-selected strong { font: 700 1.15rem/1 var(--font-display, 'Barlow Condensed', 'Arial Narrow', sans-serif); text-transform: capitalize; } .ds-slot-selected small { font-size: .74rem; line-height: 1.3; } .ds-slot-open { width: 28px; height: 28px; flex: 0 0 auto; border: 4px solid #61d27f; border-radius: 50%; }

narrative.overview:
Manggahan Active should feel like a community facility timetable drawn directly onto the playing surface: energetic, legible, and ready for action. Deep court green and warm score-sheet paper establish the system; sport-surface colors identify context, while action blue and mango are reserved for selection, direction, and active emphasis.

The system is operational rather than decorative. Strong horizontal bands, court-rule dividers, condensed athletic headings, and clear state symbols make dense availability easy to scan. Its friendliness comes from warm paper, vivid markers, direct language, and accessible controls—not soft cards or ornamental illustration.

The Courtline Scheduler is a reusable component grammar, not a mandate to reuse the Daily Scoreboard page composition. New surfaces may change their arrangement while preserving the same palette roles, typography, linework, state vocabulary, and action hierarchy. The Daily Scoreboard's exact first viewport and lane composition remain defined only in its surface brief.
keyCharacteristics: Flat, full-width operational bands separated by rules and contrast.
Condensed uppercase display type paired with a practical sans-serif body.
Sport surfaces and authored line markings used as functional context.
One bright blue primary action or selection focus at a time.
Mostly square geometry with small functional radii on controls.
Availability communicated through symbol, label, and color together.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Action blue identifies the current selection or the one primary action; do not scatter it across unrelated decoration.

rules.name: The Triple-Coded Status Rule
rules.body: Availability is never color-only: every state requires its established symbol and a readable label.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Condensed type announces; body type explains and controls. Do not set paragraphs or form values in the display face.

rules.name: The Bands, Not Cards Rule
rules.body: Build operational hierarchy with aligned fields, rails, borders, and contrasting surfaces before introducing a contained card.

rules.name: The Rule Before Shadow Rule
rules.body: Use a border, surface change, or inset line to explain hierarchy. Add a shadow only when overlap must be spatially legible.

rules.name: The Functional Radius Rule
rules.body: Round a shape only when it communicates a control, status, or circular symbol; never soften a structural panel merely to make it friendlier.

dos: Do preserve court green and score paper as the dominant light/dark relationship.
Do use action blue for the current selection and the one obvious next action.
Do pair every availability color with its established symbol and text label.
Do prefer aligned bands, grids, rules, and sport surfaces for dense operational information.
Do keep controls keyboard-visible, at least 44px tall where interactive, and respectful of reduced motion.
Do let new page compositions vary while retaining the Courtline Scheduler's durable tokens and component grammar.
donts: Don't turn the Daily Scoreboard's exact sequence or first viewport into a mandatory template for every screen.
Don't build generic rounded-card dashboards, floating glass panels, or shadow-heavy card grids.
Don't use mango, sport colors, or semantic status colors as arbitrary decoration.
Don't communicate open, limited, booked, selected, confirmed, or pending with color alone.
Don't use condensed display type for paragraphs, form values, or long instructions.
Don't introduce large corner radii on structural surfaces; 3–4px is the control language, not a suggestion to round everything.
